evidence_roles.annual_embedding: non-primary structural-change context, not direct dust concentration
evidence_roles.exposure_context: population, road, and amenity context, not confirmed direct impacts for every exposed person
evidence_roles.point_weather: short-window point-sample wind and precipitation context, not a regional maximum claim

forbidden_claims: exact casualties, hospitalizations, or measured PM concentrations are computed here
all exposed people are confirmed directly affected
annual embedding change directly measures dust concentration or visibility
hydrologic flooding is the leading response priority
required_claims: the event is an acute dust/sandstorm disruption rather than a hydrologic flood or long-term land-cover damage case
dry windy short-window meteorology supports dust transport and low visibility
population, critical amenities, and roads make air-quality, visibility, transport, and public-health response operationally important

criteria.description: Returns air_quality_visibility_transport_public_health_priority or an equivalent compact label.
criteria.name: Priority label
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for identifying dust response but omitting public health, visibility, or transport emphasis.

criteria.description: Links the dust/sandstorm hazard to airborne dust, visibility reduction, transport disruption, and respiratory or public-health concerns.
criteria.name: Dust-impact mechanism
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for identifying dust transport but not connecting it to the full operational impact pathway.

criteria.description: Uses peak wind near 22.1 km/h, Open-Meteo precipitation near 2.4 mm, NASA POWER precipitation near 2.1 mm, and ERA5-Land mean precipitation near 1.66 mm.
criteria.name: Meteorological anchors
criteria.partial_credit: 1-3 points for using some wind or precipitation metrics but missing the dry-windy contrast.

criteria.description: Uses exposure-context metrics correctly: about 11.4 million people, 89 critical amenities, and 211 road features, without treating them as confirmed direct impacts.
criteria.name: Exposure anchors
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for using one or two exposure metrics or for describing exposure qualitatively.

criteria.description: Builds the chain from dry windy surface conditions to dust transport and low visibility to public-health and transport priority.
criteria.name: Impact-chain construction
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for a partial driver-hazard-priority chain.

criteria.description: Treats annual embedding change near 0.026 as non-primary context rather than proof of long-term land-cover damage.
criteria.name: Remote-sensing context
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for mentioning annual change but not clearly separating it from acute dust impact.

criteria.description: Avoids unsupported exact casualties, hospitalization, PM concentration, airport closure, or confirmed direct-impact claims.
criteria.name: Unsupported-claim control
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for avoiding most but not all unsupported impact escalations.

evidence_roles.exposure_context: package population, road, and amenity context
evidence_roles.point_weather: short-window point-sample wind and precipitation context
